## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Mahiṁsarājacariya* (“The Conduct of the Buffalo King”) is the fifteenth narrative of the *Cariyāpiṭaka* [Catalog; Bareau, Les récits canoniques]. The text is linked thematically to the *Mahiṁsarājajātaka* (Ja 278) of the Jātaka collection. In his edition of the text, Richard Morris notes that tales such as the *Mahiṁsarājacariya* are substantially shorter than their prose Jātaka counterparts, because the compiler was primarily concerned with illustrating the moral virtue of the Bodhisatta, deliberately setting aside the humor, narrative elaboration, and entertainment of the older stories [Morris 1882].
